Built-in plugins share one registry

Roadmap, OpenAPI, and this landing are compiled into the binary and use the same registry. Project plugins: Not available in this release.

No. 06

Theming without forking

Presets, tokens, variants, and a live configurator in the shipped UI; overlay individual template files when that isn't enough.

Folio Docs

Source analysis, theming, one binary, every reader, the open platform, then more languages, migrations and the API portal. Everything that turns a repository into a published site.

v0.1Shipped

Foundation

Source analysis

Python first: source in, documented site out.

  • One command sets the project up
  • Reads your source, never runs it
  • API reference and your guides in one site
  • Types in signatures link to their pages
  • Edit a docstring, see the page
  • A component library and full-text search
  • llms.txt from day one
v0.2Shipped

Theming

Visual ownership

Own the look at any depth, then ship it anywhere static files go.

  • Presets, shareable packages, or your own template
  • Readers retheme the site from the site
  • A preview site per pull request
  • Social preview images
v0.3Shipped

One Binary

One platform

One native binary reads Python, JavaScript and Rust; the built-in plugins share one contract, and this site runs on it.

  • The core in Rust: one native binary, no Python to install
  • Three readers in the binary: Python, JavaScript, and Rust
  • Built-in plugins ship pages, components, and data
  • Your own React components in any page
  • Every project ships its authoring contract
  • Every page gets a portable Markdown mirror
  • Roadmap, landing, and OpenAPI integrations
v0.4Up next

Every Reader

Reach

One site for every reader: the language the code is in, the version they are on, and the language they read. Everything the alpha marks not available.

  • TypeScript next to JavaScript
  • Versioning — docs for every version of your library
  • Internationalization — sites in your readers' languages
  • Cross-language references
  • One search, one llms.txt, every language
  • Inline type information in examples
  • Folio's own API reference, read by its Rust reader
v0.5Later

Open Platform

Extensibility

Others extend it: project plugins return, a language is something you can add, and the beta draws its stability lines.

  • Project plugins return as sidecars over JSON-RPC
  • Language contract — a public way to add a language
  • A plugin catalog outsiders can publish into
  • Starter templates
  • Live plugin demos with their source
  • folio score — how agent-ready any docs site is
  • Agent discovery by the specs: .well-known and text/markdown negotiation
v0.6Later

More Languages

Reach

New languages arrive as parsers, not new toolchains.

  • Go, C#, and Java next to Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Rust
v0.7Later

Migrations

Adoption

Bring your existing docs over in one command, with an honest report of what didn't convert.

  • One-command import from MkDocs, Mintlify, and Read the Docs
  • Sphinx cross-links carry over
  • A theme preset that feels familiar
  • Redirects for every moved page
  • One site across products and repos
v0.8Later

API Portal

API workflow

The API portal teams expect: changelogs from real changes, and examples that cannot lie.

  • Field-level API components
  • A page per endpoint
  • Builds fail on breaking changes
  • Try requests on the page
  • SDK examples verified against the code
  • Event APIs too
